notes: LT-03.2b finite, internally linked draft/simulation/publication/history/restore oracle for two actors. It extends the immutable LT-03.2a definitions (three published versions plus the separated scenario-role universes) and the auth fixture actors. Every request/response/error body is literal data: no matcher, priority selection, name derivation, revision bump or count is computed by the validator. The `timeline` is one coherent Atlas/Nova sequence; `failures` and `replays` are explicitly isolated scenarios that declare their own preconditions. The conflict/same-target simulations use their own isolated dictionary states (draft revisions 101/102, `universe` label, no live history) and never pretend to be the live revision 2. Idempotency is user-scoped: a different actor with the same UUID is a new operation evaluated on current conditions, not a key conflict. Scenario expected action/audit IDs are recorded for LT-03.5b but are NOT audit evidence.

timeline.reason: A successful save from expected revision 0 returns revision 1 (revision + 1).
The same name in another company is allowed; no false cross-company conflict.
worker-one saves the shared draft from expected revision 1 to revision 2.
The candidate replaces only its own version over all READY Atlas items, including hidden/filtered ones and an item matched by another dictionary.
The remaining rows come from a second page with the same fixed total and counts.
The accepted publication acknowledges the specific NO_SCENARIO simulation, creates immutable version 2 and the full RuleSet; the occupied target is visible but does not block.
The published version is immutable and can be read after later edits.
worker-two saves the shared invoices draft from revision 1 to revision 2 with the exact version 2 rules before testing it.
The candidate invoices v2 draft is tested against the full set whose invoices member is still the previous active v1.
The accepted publication fixes invoices v2 in the full set and leaves the already accepted general version 2 and its history unchanged.
Restore copies version 1 into the shared draft, increments the revision and records the provenance without rewriting history.
The restored draft must pass a fresh full READY test before it can be published.
The new version 3 records restored_from_version_id = version-atlas-general-v1; the previous history is untouched.
The history contains only the dictionary's own published versions: v3, v2, v1. The scenario-role universes are never counted.
A manual edit after restore clears based_on_version_id, so the draft becomes an ordinary new candidate.
Isolated precondition: the company has zero READY items. The test is valid but warns EMPTY_READY_SET and proves no coverage.
Isolated scenario universe scenario-conflict: revision 101 carries the conflict candidate rules; equal-priority rules plan different targets, so the file is a RULE_CONFLICT manual review.

Isolated scenario universe scenario-same-target: revision 102 carries the same-target candidate rules; equal-priority rules with the same final target are not a conflict and attribution is stable dictionary_id then rule_id.
